hints: Look carefully at position. P is the round join in the middle where the four arms meet, while Q is the tiny cap right at the tip of one arm.

Remember the jobs: the middle join holds sister chromatids together for spindle attachment, while the tip cap protects the end of the DNA. A centriole is a whole separate cell organelle, not part of a chromosome.
walkthrough:
**Look at what the diagram shows**

You can see a duplicated chromosome made of sister chromatids joined together. P is labelled at the central joining point. Q is labelled at the very end of one chromatid arm.

**Identify P in the centre**

The constricted region that holds the sister chromatids together is the centromere. This is also where spindle fibres attach during mitosis. So P must be the centromere, not a centriole (a centriole is a cytoplasmic structure that organises the spindle).

**Identify Q at the tip**

The protective cap of repetitive DNA at the end of a chromatid is the telomere. It prevents loss of genes and stops ends sticking together. So Q must be the telomere, not a whole chromatid or a centriole.

options.A: Incorrect. P is not a centriole (that is a separate organelle in the cytoplasm) and Q is not a whole chromatid (a chromatid is one entire long arm).
options.B: Correct. P is the centromere that joins sister chromatids, and Q is the telomere that caps and protects the chromosome end.
options.C: Half right only. P is correctly the centromere, but Q cannot be a centriole as centrioles are not part of the chromosome structure.
options.D: Half right only. Q is correctly the telomere, but P cannot be a centriole as P is the central joining region of the chromosome.
